QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_40

question.text: Which statement about the Sharpe Ratio is TRUE?

answer.text: It uses total risk (standard deviation) in the denominator
It uses only systematic risk (beta) in the denominator
It uses downside deviation in the denominator
It uses maximum drawdown in the denominator

explanation.text: The Logic: Sharpe = (Rp − Rf) / σp. The denominator is total risk, i.e., the portfolio's standard deviation. By contrast, Treynor uses beta (systematic risk only) in its denominator. The Trap: Option B describes the Treynor Ratio. Options C and D describe other risk-adjusted measures, not the Sharpe Ratio as defined in the workbook. Note: Sharpe and Treynor differ only in their denominator (total risk vs. systematic risk), which is the workbook-supported distinction tested here.
